'''Matthew Kelly Barnes''' (born March 9, 1980) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played 14 seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He was drafted in the second round of the [[2002 NBA draft]] by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] and won an [[NBA championship]] with the [[Golden State Warriors]] in his final season in the league in 2017. Barnes is currently a basketball analyst for [[ESPN]] as well as [[NBC Sports California]] for [[Sacramento Kings]] games.

==Early life==
Barnes was born in [[Santa Clara, California]], to an Italian mother and an African American father.<ref>{{cite web|last=Hoffarth|first=Tom|date=May 12, 2012|url=http://www.insidesocal.com/tomhoffarth/2012/05/12/q-and-a-the-lak/|title=Q and A: Lakers' Matt Barnes can remember his mom through his Athletes vs. Cancer foundation|work=insidesocial.com|access-date=May 23, 2014|archive-date=May 24, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140524041448/http://www.insidesocal.com/tomhoffarth/2012/05/12/q-and-a-the-lak/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He attended [[Del Campo High School]] in [[Fair Oaks, California]], where he was a [[Letterman (sports)|letterman]] in [[American football|football]] and basketball. Barnes earned All-American, All-State, All-[[California Interscholastic Federation|CIF]], All-City, and All-League honors in each sport.<ref>{{cite web|title=#23 Matt Barnes |url=http://www.uclabruins.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/102498aac.html |work=UCLABruins.com |publisher=CBS Interactive |access-date=March 4, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120614025633/http://www.uclabruins.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/102498aac.html |archive-date=June 14, 2012 }}</ref>

Barnes played four seasons of [[college basketball]] at [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]], where he was an All-Pacific-10 Honorable Mention selection in 2001.

==Professional career==

===Fayetteville Patriots (2002–2003)===
Barnes was selected with the 46th overall pick by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in the [[2002 NBA draft]], and was immediately traded, along with [[Nick Anderson (basketball)|Nick Anderson]], to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] for [[Wesley Person]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-2002-06-27-0206270286-story.html|title=Houston, no problem|last=reporter|first=Sam Smith, Tribune pro basketball|website=chicagotribune.com|date=27 June 2002 |language=en-US|access-date=2019-10-15}}</ref> The Cavaliers assigned Barnes for the [[NBA D-League]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/CAVALIERS_SIGN_MATT_BARNES_AND-53835-44.html|title=Cavaliers Sign Matt Barnes and Smush Parker to Contracts|website=Cleveland Cavaliers|language=en|access-date=2019-10-15}}</ref> and he joined the [[Fayetteville Patriots]] for the 2002–03 season.

=== Long Beach Jam (2003–2004) ===
Barnes signed with the [[Long Beach Jam]] of the [[American Basketball Association (2000–present)|ABA]] for their inaugural season in 2003, where he played with [[Dennis Rodman]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2004-jan-17-sp-rodman17-story.html|title=Rodman, on the Rebound, Makes Jam Debut|date=2004-01-17|website=Los Angeles Times|language=en-US|access-date=2019-10-15}}</ref> The team went 24–7 and won the ABA championship.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2004-mar-10-sp-aba10-story.html|title=Long Beach Jam Wins League Title|date=2004-03-10|website=Los Angeles Times|language=en-US|access-date=2019-10-15}}</ref> Barnes averaged 18.9 points and 6.8 rebounds.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/long-beach-jammed-at-pyramid/n-3000886|title=Long Beach Jammed at Pyramid|date=2004-02-08|website=OurSports Central|language=en|access-date=2019-10-15}}</ref>

=== Los Angeles Clippers (2004) ===
Barnes signed a contract with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] for the second half of the 2003–04 NBA season.

=== Sacramento Kings (2004–2005) ===
In October 2004, Barnes signed with the [[Sacramento Kings]]. He made his debut for the Kings recording 17 points and nine rebounds, establishing himself as a key rotation player for Sacramento.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/241102006 Kings vs. Mavericks – Box Score]</ref> Barnes was traded halfway through the [[2004–05 NBA season|2004–05 season]] along with [[Chris Webber]] to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], in exchange for [[Kenny Thomas (basketball)|Kenny Thomas]], [[Corliss Williamson]] and [[Brian Skinner]]. Barnes did not suit up for Philadelphia that season while recovering from a knee tendinitis, and was given an injury release.

=== New York Knicks (2005) ===
Barnes signed a free agent contract with the [[New York Knicks]] in October 2005. Although he appeared to secure a starting job with an impressive preseason and [[Allan Houston]]'s retirement,<ref>{{cite news |title=A Scrappy Barnes Passes His Final Knicks Audition (Published 2005) |work=The New York Times |date=27 October 2005 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230129124134/https://www.nytimes.com/2005/10/27/sports/basketball/a-scrappy-barnes-passes-his-final-knicks-audition.html |archive-date=2023-01-29 |url-status=live |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2005/10/27/sports/basketball/a-scrappy-barnes-passes-his-final-knicks-audition.html |last1=Picker |first1=David }}</ref> Barnes was waived by the Knicks after playing in just six games.

=== Philadelphia 76ers (2005–2006) ===
Barnes was claimed by the 76ers to serve a second stint in Philadelphia,<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2253987 Barnes re-signs with 76ers]</ref> where he finished out the 2005–06 season.

===Golden State Warriors (2006–2008)===
Barnes signed with the [[Golden State Warriors]] before their first day of training camp in October 2006,<ref>[http://www.sacunion.com/pages/sports/articles/8543/ Kings' Matt Barnes off to Golden State] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061022152646/http://www.sacunion.com/pages/sports/articles/8543/ |date=October 22, 2006 }}</ref> and effectively raised his status in the league since joining the team. With struggling forward [[Mike Dunleavy Jr.]] placed on the bench, Barnes was given more playing time by coach [[Don Nelson]]. On December 26, 2006, Barnes hit seven [[three-point field goal]]s to tie a Warriors franchise record.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20121022215414/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=261226009 Davis (21 points, 16 assists) golden for Warriors in win]</ref> The record was broken later that season by [[Jason Richardson]], who hit eight three-pointers on March 29, 2007.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?f=/c/a/2007/03/30/SPGT1OUQDF1.DTL&hw=richardson+three&sn=015&sc=258 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071113144103/http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?f=/c/a/2007/03/30/SPGT1OUQDF1.DTL&hw=richardson+three&sn=015&sc=258 |url-status=dead |archive-date=November 13, 2007 |title=J-Rich gets healthy vs. Suns, Guard sets team record for threes |last=Hu |first=Janny |date=March 30, 2007 |work=[[San Francisco Chronicle]] |access-date=August 8, 2010}}</ref> Barnes, a high-school [[All-American]] wide receiver, says that if he had not been signed by the Warriors he would have tried out for the [[NFL]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?f=/c/a/2006/12/14/SPG4RMVILC1.DTL&hw=matt+barnes+nfl&sn=001&sc=1000 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20121216123206/http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?f=/c/a/2006/12/14/SPG4RMVILC1.DTL&hw=matt+barnes+nfl&sn=001&sc=1000 |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 16, 2012 |title=Barnes turns Warriors into believers |last1=Hu |first1=Janny |date=December 14, 2006 |work=[[San Francisco Chronicle]] |access-date=August 5, 2010}}</ref>

Before signing with Golden State, Barnes had only made 10 three-pointers in his career. In the [[2006–07 NBA season|2006–07 season]], Barnes made 106. After joining Golden State, his offense improved impressively, from 3.0 points a game in Philadelphia to 9.8, appearing in 76 games. Barnes also added a strong 2007 post-season, with 11.1 ppg and 5.7 rpg in eleven playoff games and helped the #8-seed Warriors take down the #1-seed Mavericks in the 2007 playoffs.

On August 6, 2007, Barnes returned to the Warriors under a one-year contract.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/Warriors_ReSign_Matt_Barnes.html |title=Warriors Re-Sign Free Agent Forward Matt Barnes To Contract |date=August 6, 2007 |work=[[NBA]] |access-date=August 5, 2010}}</ref> Barnes, along with teammates [[Stephen Jackson]] and [[Baron Davis]], served as a Warriors team captain for the [[2007–08 NBA season|2007–08 season]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3045549|title=Tattooed Jackson focused on future with Warriors|date=2007-10-02|website=ESPN.com|language=en|access-date=2019-10-15}}</ref> He was not expected to return for the [[2008–09 NBA season|2008–09 season]].<ref>{{cite news| url=http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?f=/c/a/2008/07/02/SPCF11ICKB.DTL | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080702203817/http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?f=/c/a/2008/07/02/SPCF11ICKB.DTL | url-status=dead | archive-date=July 2, 2008 | work=The San Francisco Chronicle | title=Later Daze, Baron: Davis leaves Warriors for Clippers | first=Janny | last=Hu | date=March 31, 2010}}</ref>

===Phoenix Suns (2008–2009)===
On July 22, 2008, Barnes signed a one-year contract with the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/news/barnes_suns_080722.html.html |title=Suns Sign Matt Barnes to One-Year Contract |work=NBA.com |date=July 22, 2008 |access-date=February 21, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Greene |first=Josh |url=http://www.nba.com/suns/news/newsroom_080722.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080731122747/http://www.nba.com/suns/news/newsroom_080722.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 31, 2008 |title=Suns Ink Barnes to a One-Year Deal |work=NBA.com |date=July 22, 2008 |access-date=February 21, 2017}}</ref> On November 14, he received a two-game suspension for his role in the scuffle with Houston's [[Rafer Alston]] two days earlier.<ref>{{cite web |last=Feigen |first=Jonathan |url=http://www.chron.com/sports/rockets/article/Rockets-Alston-to-miss-2-games-because-of-fight-1756774.php |title=Rockets' Alston to miss 2 games because of fight |work=Chron.com |date=November 14, 2008 |access-date=February 21, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Stein |first=Marc |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3702897 |title=NBA fight fallout: Nash, Alston, Barnes suspended |work=ESPN.com |date=November 14, 2008 |access-date=February 21, 2017}}</ref>

===Orlando Magic (2009–2010)===
[[File:Matt Barnes Orlando Magic (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|Barnes in 2010]]
On July 23, 2009, Barnes signed a two-year deal with the [[Orlando Magic]]. Although he was able to opt out of his deal after the first year, Barnes stated that he wanted to remain in Orlando.<ref>{{cite tweet|number=12082796500|user=Matt_Barnes22|title=@Magic_Mikey I wanna b w/the magic 4 the rest of my career luv it here. U guys let them know weather or not u want me around??<!-- full text of tweet that Twitter returned to the bot (excluding links) added by TweetCiteBot. This may be better truncated or may need expanding (TW limits responses to 140 characters) or case changes. --> |accessdate=2010-12-29|date=13 April 2010}}</ref> After the Magic were eliminated in the 2010 NBA playoffs by the [[Boston Celtics]], Barnes announced he would opt out of the final year of his contract.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://nba.fanhouse.com/2010/05/31/orlandos-matt-barnes-to-opt-out-of-his-contract-become-a-free/ |title=Orlando's Matt Barnes to Opt Out of His Contract, Become a Free Agent |last1=Pollakoff |first1=Brett |date=May 31, 2010 |work=NBA Fanhouse |access-date=August 5, 2010 |archive-date=August 10, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100810165117/http://nba.fanhouse.com/2010/05/31/orlandos-matt-barnes-to-opt-out-of-his-contract-become-a-free |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Los Angeles Lakers (2010–2012)===
On July 23, 2010, Barnes signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/los-angeles/nba/news/story?id=5403111 |title=Veteran Barnes signs with Lakers |date=July 23, 2010 |work=[[ESPN]] |access-date=August 5, 2010}}</ref>

===Return to the Clippers (2012–2015)===
[[File:Matt Barnes Los Angeles Clippers 2013 (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|150px|Barnes in 2013]]
Barnes signed with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in September 2012.<ref name=clips>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/clippers-sign-matt-barnes|title=CLIPPERS SIGN MATT BARNES|work=NBA.com|date=September 14, 2012|access-date=June 25, 2015}}</ref> On October 31, 2012, he was suspended for one game after he pleaded no contest to a misdemeanor for resisting, delaying, or obstructing a police officer.<ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.nba.com/2012/news/10/31/clippers-barnes-suspension.ap/index.html | title=Clippers' Barnes suspended for season opener | work=NBA | access-date=October 31, 2012}}</ref> In June 2013, Barnes was named Defensive Player of the Year for the Clippers.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/clippers-award-series-matt-barnes Clippers Award Series – Matt Barnes]</ref>

On July 10, 2013, Barnes re-signed with the Clippers to a multi-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/clippers-sign-matt-barnes-darren-collison-ryan-hollins-and-chris-paul|title=CLIPPERS SIGN MATT BARNES, DARREN COLLISON, RYAN HOLLINS AND CHRIS PAUL|work=NBA.com|date=July 10, 2013|access-date=June 25, 2015}}</ref> In November 2013, Barnes was fined $25,000 for not leaving the court in a timely manner after an ejection in a game against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] and for using his [[Twitter]] account during the game in violation of the NBA's rules.<ref>{{cite news|last=Turner|first=Broderick|work=Los Angeles Times|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/la-sp-clippers-20131115-story.html|title=Clippers' Matt Barnes is fined $25,000 by NBA in wake of ejection|date=2013-11-14}}</ref>

During the 2014–15 season, Barnes was fined multiple times. On December 13, he was fined $25,000 for kicking a water bottle and using language during a game against the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Rohlin|first=Melissa|work=Los Angeles Times|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/clippers/clippersnow/la-sp-cn-matt-barnes-lebron-james-jail-time-20150302-story.html|title= Matt Barnes tweets that if he'd kicked LeBron James he'd be in jail|date=2015-03-05}}</ref> On January 25, 2015, Barnes was fined $25,000 for what was said to be inappropriate language directed towards a fan during a game against the [[Phoenix Suns]], although Barnes said that it was directed towards the Suns' owner.<ref>{{cite news|last=Bolch|first=Ben|work=Los Angeles Times|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/clippers/clippersnow/la-sp-cn-nba-matt-barnes-clippers-fine-20150128-story.html|title= Clippers' Matt Barnes says fine came from exchange with Suns owner|date=2015-01-28}}</ref> On May 8, he was fined $50,000 for remarks made to [[James Harden]]'s mother during a playoff game against the Houston Rockets.<ref>{{cite news|last=Turner|first=Broderick|work=Los Angeles times|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/clippers/clippersnow/la-sp-sn-nba-fines-matt-barnes-50000-20150508-story.html|title= NBA fines Clippers' Matt Barnes $50,000 for comments to James Harden's mom|date=2015-05-08}}</ref>

===Memphis Grizzlies (2015–2016)===
On June 15, 2015, Barnes was traded, along with [[Spencer Hawes]], to the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in exchange for shooting guard [[Lance Stephenson]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Hornets Acquire Spencer Hawes and Matt Barnes from the Los Angeles Clippers in Exchange for Lance Stephenson |date=June 15, 2015 |work=NBA.com |url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/hornets-acquire-spencer-hawes-and-matt-barnes-los-angeles-clippers-exchange-lance-stephenson |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150616122948/http://www.nba.com/hornets/hornets-acquire-spencer-hawes-and-matt-barnes-los-angeles-clippers-exchange-lance-stephenson |archive-date=June 16, 2015 |url-status=live }}</ref> Ten days later, Barnes was traded again, this time to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in exchange for [[Luke Ridnour]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-acquire-matt-barnes-150625|title=Grizzlies acquire Matt Barnes from Charlotte Hornets|work=NBA.com|date=June 25, 2015|access-date=June 25, 2015}}</ref> The move reunited Barnes with the team that originally drafted him in 2002.

On December 28, 2015, Barnes was suspended by the NBA for two games for a physical altercation with [[New York Knicks]] coach [[Derek Fisher]] at the home of Barnes' estranged wife in Southern California in October.<ref>[https://sports.yahoo.com/news/sources--matt-barnes-suspended-two-games-for-altercation-with-derek-fisher-155100720.html Sources: Matt Barnes suspended two games for altercation with Derek Fisher]</ref> On January 13, 2016, the NBA Players Association filed a grievance on behalf of Barnes to get his two-game suspension without pay rescinded.<ref>[https://sports.yahoo.com/news/sources--players-association-files-grievance-on-behalf-of-grizzlies--matt-barnes--221402222.html Sources: Players association files grievance on behalf of Grizzlies’ Matt Barnes]</ref> Four days later, Barnes was fined $35,000 by the NBA for publicly defending his violence towards Fisher in their October scuffle.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nydailynews.com/sports/basketball/knicks/nba-fines-matt-barnes-35-000-condoning-violence-article-1.2499657|title=NBA fines Matt Barnes $35,000 for saying 'violence is never the answer, but sometimes it is'|last=Bondy|first=Stefan|website=nydailynews.com|date=17 January 2016 |access-date=2019-10-15}}</ref> On February 24, he scored a season-high 25 points during a 128–119 victory over the Los Angeles Lakers.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20160224/LALMEM/gameinfo.html Barnes has 25 as Grizzlies defeat Lakers 128–119]</ref> On March 11, Barnes recorded his first career triple-double with 26 points, 11 rebounds, and 10 assists in a 121–114 overtime victory over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160311/NOPMEM/gameinfo.html |title=Stephenson leads Grizzlies to 121–114 OT win over Pelicans |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2016-03-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160311112600/http://www.nba.com/games/20160311/NOPMEM/gameinfo.html |archive-date=2016-03-11 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[https://twitter.com/ESPNNBA/status/708506513749442561 Matt Barnes finishes tonight with his first career...]</ref>

===Return to Sacramento (2016–2017)===
On July 9, 2016, Barnes signed with his hometown team, the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-four-free-agents|title=Kings Sign Four Free Agents|work=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2016|access-date=July 9, 2016}}</ref> On February 20, 2017, he was waived<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-acquire-hield-evans-galloway|title=Kings Acquire Hield, Evans, Galloway, and 2017 Draft Selections|work=NBA.com|date=February 20, 2017|access-date=February 20, 2017}}</ref> to make room for the three players the Kings acquired in the [[DeMarcus Cousins]] trade.<ref>{{cite web|last=Graf|first=Dan|url=http://www.foxsports.com/nba/story/report-kings-preparing-to-release-14-year-nba-veteran-matt-barnes-022017|title=Report: Kings preparing to release 14-year NBA veteran Matt Barnes|work=FoxSports.com|date=February 20, 2017|access-date=February 21, 2017}}</ref>

===Return to Golden State (2017)===
On March 2, 2017, Barnes signed with the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/matt-barnes-signed-20170302|title=Warriors Sign Matt Barnes|work=NBA.com|date=March 2, 2017|access-date=March 2, 2017}}</ref> The Warriors' starting forward, [[Kevin Durant]], went down with an MCL injury, which left the team in need of a replacement forward. Barnes started in five games out of his 20 games played with the Warriors in the regular season.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2017/6/13/15773294/matt-barnes-warriors-nba-champion-jose-calderon-cavs|title=Matt Barnes caught a lucky break. Now he's an NBA champion|work=SBNation.com|access-date=2017-06-18}}</ref> The Warriors won the [[2017 NBA Finals]] after defeating the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in five games, giving Barnes his lone championship ring after 14 seasons in the NBA and 16 years in professional basketball. The Warriors finished the playoffs with a 16–1 record, the best postseason winning percentage in NBA history.<ref>{{cite web |date=June 14, 2017 |title=Warriors (16–1) Record Best Postseason Winning Percentage in NBA History |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2715556-warriors-16-1-record-best-postseason-winning-percentage-in-nba-history |access-date=May 10, 2018 |website=Bleacher Report}}</ref>

=== Retirement ===
On December 11, 2017, Barnes announced his retirement from the NBA via a post on [[Instagram]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/21741510/matt-barnes-retiring-nba-14-seasons|title=Matt Barnes calling it a career, says he did it his way|work=ESPN.com|date=December 11, 2017|access-date=December 11, 2017}}</ref>

==Podcasting career==
Barnes co-hosts the digital video podcast ''All the Smoke with Matt Barnes and [[Stephen Jackson]]''.<ref>{{cite news|last=Grobar|first=Matt|title= Former Laker and NBA champ Matt Barnes signs with ICM partners|url=https://deadline.com/2020/04/matt-barnes-hollywood-agency-icm-partners-all-the-smoke-1202916645/}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Ward-Henninger|first=Colin|title= Matt Barnes, Stephen Jackson unfiltered on NBA|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/matt-barnes-stephen-jackson-unfiltered-on-nba-china-the-softer-modern-game-and-overpaid-players/}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Barnes' younger brother, [[Jason Barnes|Jason]], played football in the [[Canadian Football League]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Medina|first=Mark|title=Matt Barnes Channels grief over Mothers death to support cancer screerning|url=http://lakersblog.latimes.com/lakersblog/2011/08/matt-barnes-channels-grief-over-mothers-death-to-help-with-cancer-screening.html|work=Los Angeles Times|archive-date=August 1, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170801145458/http://lakersblog.latimes.com/lakersblog/2011/08/matt-barnes-channels-grief-over-mothers-death-to-help-with-cancer-screening.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Barnes was married to Gloria Govan, who appeared in VH1's ''[[Basketball Wives]]'' and ''[[Basketball Wives: LA]]'', and they have identical twin boys. Barnes was arrested in 2010 on suspicion of domestic violence against Govan, and for driving with a suspended license and threatening a police officer in July 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tate |first=Amethyst |date=2012-07-31 |title=Lakers' Matt Barnes Arrested Twice In Less Than Two Years |url=https://www.ibtimes.com/lakers-matt-barnes-arrested-twice-less-two-years-734545 |access-date=2019-10-15 |website=International Business Times}}</ref> They separated in 2014.<ref>[http://www.tmz.com/2014/10/14/matt-barnes-separated-from-gloria-govan-trust-issues/ NBA STAR MATT BARNES SEPARATED FROM GLORIA GOVAN... 'Trust Issues']</ref> Barnes was charged with assault on February 1, 2017 after he allegedly choked a woman and struck her boyfriend.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-02-01 |title=Matt Barnes surrenders to cops over nightclub brawl {{!}} New York Post |url=https://nypost.com/2017/02/01/matt-barnes-surrenders-to-cops-over-nightclub-brawl/ |access-date=2026-09-03 |language=en-US}}</ref>

His fiancée Anansa Sims, is the daughter of model [[Beverly Johnson]]. Sims and Barnes have two children together.<ref>{{cite web | last=Vasquez | first=Ingrid | title=Matt Barnes and Anansa Sims Welcome Second Baby Together, Son Austin: 'Love You So Much' | website=People.com | date=2024-10-03 | url=https://people.com/matt-barnes-anansa-sims-welcome-second-baby-together-son-austin-8723138 | access-date=2025-11-29}}</ref> Barnes and Sims married in 2026.
